Koh Samui is hilly, rising to 635 m at Khao Pom, but it has very few marked trails. The rewarding walks are short climbs to waterfalls (Na Muang 2 in 20–40 minutes each way; Hin Lad in about 2 hours return) and to viewpoints such as Khao Hua Jook Chedi above Chaweng, Overlap Stone above Lamai (about 300 THB including a drink) and the Secret Buddha Garden, plus free roadside lookouts like Lad Koh. Start before 10:00, carry 2 litres of water, and expect slippery trails from October to December.

Below are the 12 walks and lookouts we think are worth the effort, sorted by type, with fees, walking times, the best light and an honest note on difficulty. Most visitors combine two or three of them in a morning, then cool off at a beach or on a boat in the afternoon.

Map of walks and viewpoints

The east coast lookouts (Lad Koh, Khao Hua Jook) face sunrise. The interior walks (Na Muang 2, the Secret Buddha Garden, Pra Buddha Dipankara) are on the central ridge. Hin Lad is on the west slope above Nathon, and Laem Sor is on the south coast. The map shows the viewpoints; the table below adds coordinates for every stop.

Viewpoints you can drive to

These need little or no walking, so they suit families, hot afternoons and anyone with a scooter. Most are free.

Lad Koh

Lad Koh is a free, 24-hour roadside lookout on the ring road between Chaweng Noi and Coral Cove (9.4990, 100.0600). Steps lead down from a small car park to a platform with shrines, benches and a wide view south over the rocks and bay; a van usually sells drinks and coconut ice cream. It is a 10–15 minute stop. Parking is tight and fills fast with tour vans, and the road has blind bends, so slow down well before you turn in. Stay on the platform: in November 2024 a 24-year-old Russian visitor was swept off the rocks below by 2–3 m waves and drowned, and the municipality then closed access to the rocks. Full guide: Lad Koh viewpoint.

Khao Hua Jook Chedi

A golden chedi on a hill north of Chaweng Lake (9.5371, 100.0589), lit up at night. The terrace looks over Chaweng Lake, the airport runway and the east coast, and if you time it right you can watch planes take off below you. Turn uphill off Chaweng Lake Road and either walk the last steep stretch or ride up slowly. It is a working temple: free entry, donations welcome, shoulders and knees covered. Go at sunrise or after dark for the lights.

Chaweng Lake viewpoint

The inland road that climbs above Chaweng Lake has pull-outs with views over the lake to the sea, best in the softer light of 08:00–10:00. There is no facility and no fee; just pull fully off the road. Combine it with Khao Hua Jook and breakfast in Chaweng.

Big Buddha platform

The 12 m golden Buddha at Wat Phra Yai sits on Koh Fan, a small islet joined to the north-east coast by a causeway (9.5708, 100.0598). It is open 07:00–18:30 and free. Climb the dragon staircase for a view across Bang Rak bay to Koh Phangan; late afternoon gives the warmest light. Shoes off on the upper terrace and cover up. See our Big Buddha guide.

Laem Sor and Khao Chedi

Laem Sor Pagoda is a gold-tiled chedi right on the shore at the end of Bang Kao beach (9.4117, 99.9690), open 07:00–18:00 and free. A white chedi, Khao Chedi, stands on the hill to the west. We have not verified a public footpath up to it, so we don't publish a route; ask at the temple. The seafront chedi itself is worth 30–45 minutes, ideally in late-afternoon light. See Laem Sor Pagoda.

Short hikes

These are proper walks: short, but steep, hot and slippery in places. Wear closed shoes and carry water.

Na Muang 2

The island's hardest short walk and its tallest waterfall, about 80 m over at least five tiers (9.4723, 99.9905; open 09:00–18:00). From the top car parks take the left-hand path, signed as a free jungle walk, cross the wooden bridge and climb 20–40 minutes on roots and boulders with fixed ropes. It fills by about 10:30. At least four visitors have died in falls here since 2019, all on wet rock on the upper tiers, so stay behind the edges and skip it after heavy rain. Step-by-step route: Na Muang 2 waterfall.

Hin Lad

A quieter forest walk on the west side, starting beside a forest temple 2–3 km inland from Nathon (9.5205, 99.9556). The path follows a stream past several small tiers and pools; walking between tiers takes 30–45 minutes, and the round trip with a swim is about 2 hours. No official fee or hours are published. Details: Hin Lad Waterfall.

Overlap Stone

A privately run viewpoint on the hill above Maret, about 3 km from Lamai (9.4597, 100.0301), open 08:00–18:00. The fee is about 300 THB including a soft drink in recent reports, up from 200 THB earlier in 2026. A walk of about 500 m ends with a suspension bridge to two balanced boulders with views over Lamai. Parts have no railings. The access road is very steep near the top. Skip the chained-elephant feeding on the way up. The neighbouring "Overlap Stone 2" has been closed since a forestry raid on 22 July 2026. More: Overlap Stone.

Na Muang 1

Not a hike so much as a pleasant 5–10 minute shaded walk to an 18 m fall and a swimmable pool. It is the obvious warm-up or cool-down for Na Muang 2. See Na Muang Waterfalls 1 and 2.

The highlands: Secret Buddha Garden and the central ridge

Samui's interior is a ridge of durian and rubber smallholdings, forest and steep concrete roads. The two places worth the climb are the Secret Buddha Garden and Pra Buddha Dipankara.

  • Secret Buddha Garden (Tarnim Magic Garden): a sculpture garden begun in 1976 by a local farmer and opened to visitors after he died in 1990, now run by his family (9.4829, 99.9945; 09:00–18:00; 100 THB in recent reports, some sources still say 80 THB). The road up is very steep and narrow, with a rough final stretch: go by 4x4 or on a jungle safari, not on a rental scooter. Inside, allow 30–60 minutes on rocky, sometimes wet paths. Full guide: Secret Buddha Garden.
  • Pra Buddha Dipankara: a simple hilltop temple with statues, shrines and a wide view over the island (9.5020, 100.0060). The road is rough and steep: 4x4 is best, and scooters manage it only in the dry season with an experienced rider. Stop on the way down to let your brakes cool. Monks may ask for a donation for upkeep.
  • Khao Pom (635 m): the island's highest point. We have found no public, marked trail to the summit, so we publish no route. Don't attempt it on unmarked farm tracks without a local guide.

Good to know: the steep hill roads are where many of Samui's scooter crashes happen. Going down is more dangerous than going up. If you are not an experienced rider, take a 4x4 taxi or a tour. Read Koh Samui roads before you ride inland.

Beach and headland walks

Samui's coast is broken by granite headlands, and a few short shore walks are worth doing.

  • Choeng Mon to Koh Fan Noi: at low tide a sandbar joins Choeng Mon beach to the small island of Koh Fan Noi. Walk across only on a falling tide and come back well before the water returns, or you can be cut off. Check the tide first: [kp_tide_now] Full tables on Koh Samui tides.
  • Silver Beach and Coral Cove: the boulder-framed coves between Chaweng Noi and Lamai are good for short scrambles and snorkelling. Use water shoes on the coarse sand and keep off the rocks when there is surf. See Silver Beach and Coral Cove.
  • Hin Ta and Hin Yai: a short walk through a lane of stalls to the famous rocks at the south end of Lamai. Climbing the formations is discouraged by locals; enjoy them from the paths. See Hin Ta and Hin Yai.

All east-coast rocks are dangerous in the October–December monsoon swell. If the sea is white, stay on the sand.

Two half-day walking routes

Because most walks are short, the best way to make a morning of it is to string two or three together by car or scooter.

South: waterfalls and the mummified monk

  1. 08:30 Na Muang 1: a quick look at the pool while it is quiet.
  2. 08:50 Drive to the top car parks and climb Na Muang 2 on the left-hand path (1.5–2 h return with a rest).
  3. 11:00 Back down to Na Muang 1 for a swim to cool off.
  4. 12:00 Wat Khunaram on Route 4169, then lunch.

East: sunrise lookouts and the coves

  1. 06:00 Sunrise at Lad Koh (see the sunrise times by month below).
  2. 07:00 Short scramble and swim at Silver Beach before it fills.
  3. 09:00 Overlap Stone above Maret as it opens.
  4. 10:15 Hin Ta and Hin Yai, then breakfast or an early lunch in Lamai.

On the west side, pair Hin Lad at 08:30 with lunch in Nathon.

Walking with children

The easiest walks for families are Na Muang 1 (5–10 minutes, flat, with a pool at the end), Lad Koh, the Big Buddha steps and the Hin Ta and Hin Yai stall lane. Overlap Stone and the Secret Buddha Garden work for older children who can be trusted near drops without railings. Na Muang 2 and the upper part of Hin Lad are not suitable for young children. Carry more water than you think, start early and plan a swim at the end. More ideas in Koh Samui with kids.

Guided jungle treks and 4x4 tours

Because marked trails are rare, a guided tour is the practical way to reach the highlands. The common market product is a 4x4 jungle safari of about 7 hours (roughly 10:00–17:00, around 1,700 THB in 2026) that combines Hin Ta and Hin Yai, a swim at Na Muang, Wat Khunaram, the Secret Buddha Garden, a hilltop lunch and the Big Buddha. Private versions let you add a longer walk. For hill tracks with an engine, guided ATV rides run 1–2 hours from about 1,490 THB per rider. Ask us on WhatsApp for a shared or private option: [kp_wa]

The Samui Trail race

Samui Trail is the island's ITRA-listed trail race, with 15 km, 25 km and 55 km courses on the hill tracks. The 2025 edition ran on 8–9 November 2025; its 25 km course measured about 27 km with roughly 1,670 m of climbing and started at 05:00. Its date shows what is possible on Samui's ridges, but the race uses private land and marshalled tracks that are not open trails the rest of the year. The 2026 date had not been published when we checked. [check]

Best time and heat

Samui is hot all year: daytime highs run from 29 °C in December–February to 33 °C in May–June, with high humidity. Walk early, between sunrise (about 06:00–06:40, depending on the month) and 10:00, or after 16:00. The driest, firmest trails are February–April; waterfalls are best October–January, when trails are muddiest.

Safety on the trails

  • Water and heat: carry at least 2 litres per person for any walk over an hour. Heat exhaustion is the most common problem on Samui walks. Rest in the shade if you feel dizzy or stop sweating.
  • Slippery rock: wet granite and roots are treacherous after rain. Never step backwards for a photo near a drop; that is how the Na Muang 2 deaths happened.
  • Flash floods: October–December downpours can raise streams within minutes. Leave the stream bed if the water rises or turns brown.
  • Snakes and insects: watch where you put your hands and feet, and wear repellent; dengue is present in Thailand year-round.
  • Tell someone your route: mobile signal is patchy in the valleys. Share your plan and expected return time.
  • Waves on coastal rocks: at Lad Koh a visitor was swept off the rocks in November 2024. Stay off wave-washed rocks whenever there is swell.
  • Emergency numbers: ambulance 1669, police 191, Tourist Police 1155. Know your nearest hospital and check your travel insurance covers hiking.

What to wear and bring

  • Trail shoes or strapped sports sandals with a lugged sole (no flip-flops)
  • 2 litres of water per person, plus electrolyte sachets from 7-Eleven
  • Light, quick-dry clothing and a hat
  • Insect repellent (DEET or picaridin) and sunscreen
  • Swimwear and a small towel for the waterfall pools
  • A sarong or shirt to cover shoulders and knees at temples
  • Cash in small notes for parking, fees and drinks
  • A charged phone with offline maps and the emergency numbers saved
  • Flip-flops on any trail with ropes
  • Drones over temples or crowds without permission
  • Valuables left on rocks or in scooter baskets

Sunrise and sunset viewpoints

Samui's east coast faces sunrise and its west coast faces sunset. For sunrise, the best walking-distance lookouts are Lad Koh, Khao Hua Jook Chedi and the rocks at Silver Beach; sunrise is about 06:00–06:42 depending on the month. For sunset, head west: Taling Ngam, Lipa Noi and Nathon pier look straight out to sea, with sunset between about 17:56 and 18:45 through the year. Our sunset spots guide compares 12 places, and the waterfalls guide has a full-day route that ends at Hin Ta and Hin Yai.

The best view of all is at sea

The most famous viewpoint near Samui isn't on Samui at all. On Koh Wua Talab in Ang Thong National Marine Park, a steep staircase of 20–30 minutes climbs to a lookout over dozens of limestone islands, and it is a stop on our Ang Thong speedboat day tour (1,800 THB adult, 1,400 THB child; park fee 300 THB adult and 150 THB child, cash, not included). The park closes every year from 1 November to 15 December and reopens on 16 December 2026; our sister site angthongmarinepark.com has the full guide to the park's viewpoints.

Until then, the southern islands run every day: the Pig Island speedboat tour costs 1,450 THB adult and 1,250 THB child, with snorkelling at Koh Tan. Hotel transfers are included from the main areas; remote areas pay a surcharge, which we confirm when you book.
